raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

Companion LMCache PR: https://github.com/LMCache/LMCache/pull/5985 ("[MP][vLLM] End reloads on the engine's reusable boundary"). Each PR is inert without the other.

## Overview

This is a correctness fix for the prefix cache of align-mode Mamba models under speculative decoding.

Under the EAGLE block drop, a GPU prefix hit resumes from the Mamba state one block below the match end. A KV
connector that loads up to its longest match restores the Mamba state *at* the match end, a state that no request can
ever hit. Once the reusable state (one block lower) has been evicted from the GPU, every request misses, every request
reloads the same unreachable state, and nobody prefills locally to re-create the reusable one: the GPU prefix cache can
never recover. Measured on Kimi-K3 (MLA + KDA) + DSpark K=7: 0 % GPU prefix hit at concurrency 48 and 64, for the whole
run.

Under the EAGLE block drop, a reload must therefore end on a boundary vLLM can reuse. This PR lets vLLM tell the
connector, as data, where a load must end to be reusable (`get_reusable_load_rule()`, built on the existing checkpoint
rule), and retains the Mamba state a negotiated load ends on, so a reload re-creates a GPU-hittable state and the prefix cache recovers by
itself. The fix does not depend on a throughput gain; the benchmark below is reported as measured.

## Claims

- New connector-facing API: `KVConnectorBase_V1.get_reusable_load_rule() -> (granularity_tokens, drop_tokens) | None`
  (delegates to `KVCacheManager` / `KVCacheCoordinator`): a load for a match of `n` tokens should end at
  `max(n // granularity * granularity - drop, 0)`, the position of the existing
  `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(..., drop_eagle_block=True)`; `None` when every load end is reusable. And
  `KVConnectorBase_V1.ends_loads_on_reusable_boundary` (default `False`). About 60 lines of code.
- When a connector declares it, the scheduler retains the Mamba state at the end of each completed connector load
  (one more reachable boundary for the sparse prefix-cache retention), so the next request hits it on the GPU.
- No behaviour change for any connector that does not set the flag, or for models without align-mode Mamba under the
  EAGLE block drop (the API returns `None`). `VLLM_MAMBA_CACHE_CONNECTOR_LOAD_STATE=0` turns the retention off.
- End to end with the companion LMCache PR on Kimi-K3 + DSpark K=7, 8x MI355X: the GPU prefix cache recovers by
  itself (GPU prefix hit 0 % -> 53-55 % at concurrency 48 / 64), LMCache reloads fall 61 % (306 M -> 119 M retrieved
  tokens over concurrency 32-64), and the reusable junction states are re-created after every eviction (0 -> 378 / 462
  re-stores at 48 / 64). TTFT and throughput are not better yet; see Validation for why (duplicate concurrent loads)
  and the follow-up.

## Validation

**Functional (F0, GPU, scripted traffic, random-token 63,240-token prefix + distinct suffixes, ISL 68,000):**
with this revision of both PRs (their diffs on the benchmark build; F0_PASS):
P1 = prefix + suffix 1 prefilled locally (LMCache stores); `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; P2 = prefix + suffix 2 on a
cold GPU: the server decides `case1 engine_hit=0 longest=61440 returned=61440 match=62976`, LMCache loads exactly
61,440 tokens, and the KV events show the junction state (block 39) stored in all 3 KDA groups at the load end; P3 =
prefix + suffix 3: GPU prefix hit 61,440 tokens; P2 again (GPU path) gives identical greedy output. The first run of
this check found that applying the rule to LMCache's longest *servable* length takes the drop twice when the recurrent
state is missing at the match end (single-request prefill stores KDA states every 3,072 tokens, so servable 61,440 <
match 62,976 -> the server returned 58,368); the rule now maps the token match (full-attention rows), covered by unit
tests.

**Benchmark** (customer harness, 8 shared 63,240-token prefixes, ISL 68,000 / OSL 350, 93 % cache, seed 20261020;
same command and memory settings as the baseline; baseline = same vLLM build and LMCache without this change):

| conc | TTFT p50 (s) baseline -> this | TTFT p90 (s) | ITL p50 (ms) | out tok/s/GPU | GPU prefix hit | running avg / max |
|---:|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 9.31 -> 9.85 | 18.15 -> 17.76 | 42.1 -> 40.4 | 51.6 -> 50.7 | 64.9 % -> 85.7 % | 20.0 / 32 -> 19.8 / 32 |
| 48 | 16.05 -> 15.82 | 25.15 -> 26.63 | 53.0 -> 68.5 | 52.8 -> 48.6 | **0.0 % -> 53.0 %** | 26.4 / 36 -> 30.6 / 46 |
| 64 | 29.30 -> **24.62** | 34.78 -> 40.32 | 58.2 -> 80.6 | 53.2 -> 48.4 | **0.0 % -> 55.0 %** | 27.8 / 36 -> 35.4 / 51 |

Baseline: the same vLLM build and LMCache without these changes (same command, `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.9`, L2
page-cached). Concurrency 16 is the cold first point of the sweep and is not compared. The benchmark ran the same vLLM change on a `df3bd094`-based ROCm build (the image the baseline used), not on the `origin/main` port, and an earlier revision of both PRs (same rule and load selection; since then the API returns the rule as data and the LMCache handshake was reduced to the rule alone) with the LMCache rule before the token-match fix (it differs on 11 of the 891 benchmark decisions, where the servable length was 61,440 and the old rule returned 58,368 / 59,904 instead of 61,440); F0 ran on the final code. KV events: in the baseline the
junction (block-39) KDA states are evicted and never re-stored (0 re-stores, no prefix with a usable junction state for
100 % of point 48); with the handshake they are re-stored after every eviction (378 / 462 re-stores at 48 / 64, a
removed -> re-stored gap of p50 5.4 s / 10 s), and some prefix always has one. The server decided 155 + 193 case1
(GPU already at the junction, the usual one-chunk load) and 120 + 199 case2 (reload ends at 61,440) at 48 / 64.

LMCache retrieved tokens (server counters, `lmc_ops`): 24.1 / 120.9 / 161.2 M -> 5.8 / 50.1 / 63.0 M at 32 / 48 / 64
(-61 % in total).

**What the benchmark shows, and what remains.** The fix does what it must: the GPU prefix cache recovers (0 % ->
53-55 % at 48 / 64), LMCache reloads fall 61 %, and the junction states are re-created after every eviction. TTFT and
throughput are not better yet (TTFT p50 -16 % at 64 but p90 +16 %; ITL p50 +29-38 % and output tok/s/GPU -8-9 % at
48 / 64; one run, no repeats). The cause is a separate, pre-existing issue that the fix now exposes: the junction
state is still evicted under KV pressure (it is an ordinary evictable cached block), and when that happens every
waiting request with the same prefix misses on the GPU and starts its **own** connector load of the same blocks. Each
of them then holds a private copy of the 61k-token prefix (KV pool back near 100 %, more requests running at once:
max 46-51 vs 36), which is what costs ITL and throughput. Before this fix the same herd existed but stayed stuck at
0 % GPU hit; now each herd ends with a GPU-hittable state.

The follow-up is a separate vLLM PR (independent of this one, connector-agnostic): **single-flight connector loads**,
so a block hash is never loaded into HBM while a copy of it is already resident or in flight, and requests with the
same prefix wait for one load instead of each loading their own.

**Unit tests (CPU):** new `tests/v1/core/prefix_cache/test_connector_load_boundary.py` (the rule vs
`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position`, `None` without align Mamba / EAGLE drop, retention only when the connector
declares it, kill switch, `MultiConnector` delegation). Touched suites base (`origin/main`) vs this branch:
`tests/v1/core/test_prefix_caching.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_single_type_kv_cache_manager.py tests/v1/core/prefix_cache tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_multi_connector.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_cache_pollution_prevention.py tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_invalid_blocks_correctness.py`
on CPU (ROCm image with compiled ops from `df3bd094`, Python tree of each revision copied over it): base 644 passed /
57 failed, this branch 660 passed / 57 failed (16 new tests, all pass), **0 new failures**. The 57 failures are the same
on both and environmental (offline host without the `llava-hf/llava-1.5-7b-hf` config: 55 x `test_scheduler`
`ModelConfig` / `VllmConfig` validation, 1 in `test_multi_connector.py`, and the collection error of
`test_hybrid_prefix_cache_hit_rate.py`, which needs `orjson`). Lint: ruff 0.14.0 and typos 1.43.5 (pinned pre-commit
versions) clean on the changed files.

## Details

**Root cause.** Prefix match on the GPU ends at `N`; under the EAGLE block drop a hit resumes from the prefill
checkpoint one block below (`get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position(..., drop_eagle_block=True)`). Align-mode Mamba
states exist only at prefill step ends and are kept sparsely. When the junction state (end of block `N/B - 1`) is
evicted, every request misses on the GPU; the connector asks for the longest external match `M` and loads the Mamba
state at `M`, which the EAGLE-dropped hit never uses, and nobody prefills locally anymore, so the junction state is
never re-created. Measured on the baseline: GPU prefix hit 64.9 % at concurrency 32, 0.0 % at 48 and 64, at most 36
requests running, and every request holds a private copy of the 63k prefix.

**Design.**
- Single source of truth stays in vLLM: the connector does not re-implement the EAGLE / checkpoint rule, it reads
  `get_reusable_load_rule()` (bound through the existing `bind_kv_cache_manager`). The rule is returned as data
  (`granularity`, `drop`) so a connector, or the cache server behind it, can apply it without calling back into vLLM
  per request; `None` means every load end is reusable. A unit test checks the rule against
  `get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position` for every length.
- Retention is tied to the connector's declaration, not to "any connector": other connectors stay byte-identical.
- The LMCache side sends the rule to the LMCache server at startup (only the rule); the server applies it inside its
  one lookup per request. Other connectors (Mooncake, NIXL, offloading) can use the same
  API.

**Trade-offs / limitations.** A negotiated reload ends one block earlier, so that request prefills one extra block
(1,536 tokens) locally; later requests hit on the GPU. Only align-mode Mamba under the EAGLE block drop is affected.

**Files:** `vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/base.py`, `.../multi_connector.py`,
`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_coordinator.py`, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_manager.py`, `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`,
`vllm/v1/core/single_type_kv_cache_manager.py`, `vllm/v1/request.py`, `vllm/envs.py`, tests.

detail.title: [Bugfix][Core][KV Connector] Reusable-load handshake for align-mode Mamba under the EAGLE block drop

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,192 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""The end of a KV connector load as a retained Mamba "align" checkpoint.
+
+Sparse prefix-cache retention keeps a Mamba state only at proven reuse points
+(replay boundary, shared-prefix junction). vLLM tells a connector, through
+``get_reusable_load_rule``, where a load must end to stay hittable under the
+EAGLE block drop; for a connector that declares it ends its loads there, the
+scheduler also marks the end of each completed load, so the next request of
+that prefix can hit the loaded state. ``VLLM_MAMBA_CACHE_CONNECTOR_LOAD_STATE=0``
+turns the marking off.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests.v1.core.test_prefix_caching import (
+    _make_hybrid_kv_cache_config,
+    make_kv_cache_manager,
+    make_request,
+)
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.base import KVConnectorBase_V1
+from vllm.distributed.kv_transfer.kv_connector.v1.multi_connector import (
+    MultiConnector,
+)
+from vllm.utils.hashing import sha256
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_utils import init_none_hash
+from vllm.v1.core.sched.scheduler import Scheduler
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import get_mamba_prefill_checkpoint_position
+
+BLOCK = 16
+FULL, MAMBA = 0, 1
+PROMPT = list(range(1, 10 * BLOCK + 4))
+LOAD_END = 6 * BLOCK
+
+
+def _manager(spec_types=("full", "mamba"), use_eagle=True):
+    init_none_hash(sha256)
+    config = _make_hybrid_kv_cache_config(BLOCK, 1024, list(spec_types))
+    return make_kv_cache_manager(
+        kv_cache_config=config,
+        max_model_len=1 << 16,
+        enable_caching=True,
+        hash_block_size=BLOCK,
+        use_eagle=use_eagle,

+def _load_then_prefill(manager, request, load_end, boundary):
+    """A connector load of ``load_end`` tokens, then the local rest of the prompt."""
+    blocks, local, junction = manager.get_computed_blocks(request)
+    request.shared_prefix_boundary = junction
+    assert (
+        manager.allocate_slots(
+            request,
+            0,
+            num_new_computed_tokens=local,
+            new_computed_blocks=blocks,
+            num_external_computed_tokens=load_end - local,
+            delay_cache_blocks=True,
+        )
+        is not None
+    )
+    request.num_computed_tokens = load_end
+    request.connector_load_boundary = boundary
+    manager.cache_blocks(request, load_end)
+    state = manager.coordinator.single_type_managers[MAMBA].req_to_blocks[
+        request.request_id
+    ][load_end // BLOCK - 1]
+    loaded_state_cached = state.block_hash is not None
+
+    num_new = request.num_tokens - load_end
+    assert manager.allocate_slots(request, num_new) is not None
+    request.num_computed_tokens += num_new
